claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to check if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex!

To help determine your eligibility, could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 19, there are some specific circumstances where you might still be eligible for Child Benefit.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training, such as:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to Level 3
- An approved unpaid training course (not a higher education course like a university degree)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in approved education - doing A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you.

Could you tell me when Alex started their A-level course, and when is it expected to finish? Also, has Alex remained in approved education continuously since turning 16, or was there a gap at any point?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has been in education continuously since turning 16, no gaps. He started his A-levels when he was 17 and is still doing them now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the picture:

Is Alex living with you, or do you contribute to the cost of their care (for example, by paying for their food or accommodation)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. One more important question:

Are you (or your partner, if applicable) responsible for Alex? In other words, are you the person who is primarily responsible for his care and upbringing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex's other parent also lives with him and they already claim Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that important detail.

Unfortunately, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time. Since Alex's other parent is already receiving Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to make a separate claim for Alex while that existing claim is active.

If you believe you should be the one receiving the Child Benefit instead (for example, if you are the primary carer), you could discuss with Alex's other parent about transferring the claim to you. However, you cannot both claim Child Benefit for the same child simultaneously.

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify about Child Benefit?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've now completed my assessment. To summarise:

**Eligibility Outcome for Alex: Not Eligible**

**Reasoning:** Although Alex meets the age and education criteria for Child Benefit (he's 19, in approved education doing A-levels, has been in continuous education since 16, and lives with you), you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for him because his other parent is already claiming it.

**Key rule:** Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any one time. Duplicate claims for the same child are not permitted.

**Your options:**
- If circumstances change and you become the sole or primary carer, you could apply for the Child Benefit to be transferred to you
- You could discuss with Alex's other parent if they agree to stop their claim so you could claim instead

Is there anything else I can help you with?
